name: The Rootbound Chapel
region_detail: Deep in the forest, beside an overgrown path formerly used by woodland travelers.
site_type: chapel | Ancient sites; supernatural sites | Abandoned stone chapel.
history: The chapel was constructed beside an old woodland route by a community whose identity is no longer remembered. As the route fell into disuse, immense trees grew around the building, their roots gradually enclosing its walls. Local families continued to leave small offerings long after the last regular services ceased.
current_state: The roof has partially collapsed, but the altar remains intact beneath a canopy of intertwined roots. Fresh bread and flowers occasionally appear outside the entrance. On certain holy days, a single candle burns upon the altar despite the apparent absence of an attendant.
inhabitants: Woodland wildlife; occasional visitors leaving offerings. The identity of any regular attendant or supernatural occupant remains undetermined.
danger_level: Low ordinarily; uncertain if the altar, offerings, or enclosing roots are disturbed.
points_of_interest:
Root-enclosed entrance; intact altar; weathered carvings; collapsed vestry; candle niche; small collection of offerings; stone floor disappearing beneath living roots.

Unresolved elements: The identity of the chapel’s builders and the tradition it originally served; Who leaves the offerings and tends the candle, if anyone; Whether the roots protect, imprison, or merely surround the building; The nature of the spaces beneath the collapsed vestry.
discovery: Deep in the forest, beside an overgrown path formerly used by woodland travelers. Briarhearth foresters know fragments of the older woodland route. Sela Hallow may be familiar with the traditions surrounding the offerings.
related_records:
